name: Tahath
overview: Tahath was a male descendant of the tribe of Ephraim, specifically identified as the son of Eleadah. He is noted as a grandson within the lineage of Ephraim and is distinguished from another son of Ephraim with the same name. According to the biblical record, Tahath was killed by the men of Gath, marking a notable event in his life.
namesAndTitles: The name Tahath means "compensation" in Hebrew. It is a proper name mentioned in 1 Chronicles 7:20, and there is no indication that it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Tahath as the son of Eleadah. Beyond this, no other family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Tahath's significance lies in his place within the genealogical records of the tribe of Ephraim, serving as a link in the lineage through Eleadah. The mention of his death at the hands of the men of Gath highlights the ongoing conflicts faced by the descendants of Ephraim. His presence in the biblical genealogy underscores God's providential preservation of His people despite such adversities.
